First listed 2025-09-01 · episode or wrap

Steve Eisman Answers YOUR Investing Questions | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 23

Eisman explains a story-driven investing process grounded in independent data, pricing power, balance sheets and long holding periods. He favors US index exposure and AI, rejects stock compensation as economically free, and revisits MLP financing failures. The housing lock-in mechanism and several accounting principles are sound, but mortgage arithmetic exaggerates the required price decline. His account of deposit rates and the Fed constitutional origin is wrong, and EU trade authority is oversimplified. These explanatory errors are separated from untested long-term portfolio preferences and personal disclosures.

YouTube · 2025-09-01 ↗Substack · 2025-09-01 ↗
Entire transcript read. Useful company-level accounting and risk principles coexist with weaker monetary/legal explanations. Strong long-term US enthusiasm has no precise return target. The viewer recovery context runs five years, so no premature performance grade is assigned. Unverified anecdotes and portfolio disclosures remain unverified, not adverse grades.

How he reasons here

  • Require a company story beyond cheap valuation.
  • Cross-check management narratives with independent operating data.
  • Analyze cash retention, leverage and security rights together.
  • Treat stock compensation as an economic transfer.
  • Recognize personal timing and lifestyle constraints in portfolio design.
  • Watch for unsupported macro certainty and arithmetic shortcuts.
